Paragraph:
Translation: Then, Lord Krsna blew His conchshell, called Pancajanya; Arjuna blew his, the Devadatta; and Bhima, the voracious eater and performer of Herculean tasks, blew his terrific conchshell called Paundram.

Purport (Excerpt): Lord Krsna is referred to as Hrsikesa in this verse because He is the owner of all senses... Here on the Battlefield of Kuruksetra the Lord directly controls the transcendental senses of Arjuna... So, the particular types of conchshell blown by the different personalities on the side of the Pandavas, beginning with the Lord's, were all very encouraging to the fighting soldiers. On the other side there were no such credits... So, they were predestined to lose...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The leadership of the Pandava army actively steps up to counter the opposing forces and encourage their own soldiers.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Each leader blows their specifically named, powerful conchshell. The naming of the shells and the specific epithets used for the heroes highlight their individual identities, past victories, and divine empowerment.
Outcome/Resolution: The sounds serve to deeply encourage the Pandava soldiers and establish the formidable, distinct identities of their champions, contrasting with the nameless, collective noise of the Kauravas.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Svadharma (Living in alignment with one's unique nature and duty)
Hrsikesa (The concept of the Divine as the master and director of one's senses and mind)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The naming of the conchshells signifies that in the realm of dharma, individual identity is not lost but empowered by the Divine. Krishna acting as 'Hrsikesa' (master of senses) shows that when a person surrenders their actions to the Supreme, their senses are perfectly controlled and directed toward righteous victory.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse demonstrates the psychological power of individual identity and purposeful action. Unlike the Kauravas' mob mentality, the Pandava leaders act as distinct, self-actualized individuals (symbolized by their named conchshells and titles). This clear sense of self and divine backing serves as a massive psychological anchor, providing profound encouragement and resilience to their followers.
